docs.title: API contracts
docs.text:
Each component owns its contracts in its own folder:

contracts/
└── components/
    └── <component>/
        ├── openapi.yaml    # HTTP API (optional)
        ├── events.yaml     # event bus messages (optional)
        ├── internal.md     # internal interfaces (optional)
        └── examples/       # JSON examples (optional)
            ├── request-replan.json
            ├── replan-saved.json
            └── replan-conflict.json

Use one folder per component, named c<NN>-<component-name>, for example c03-resource-management or c07-disruption-detection.

docs.title: Which files a component needs
docs.text:
The architecture uses three kinds of connection, and each one has its own file. Every file is optional. Add only the ones that apply to your component.

File Use it for Example openapi.yaml HTTP operations: commands and queries from the browser (C01) or external clients C03 resource registration events.yaml Messages published to or consumed from the event bus (RabbitMQ) C06 publishes CityStateUpdated internal.md Calls from one component to another inside the same backend process, with no HTTP in between C07 calls C05 requestReplan examples/ JSON examples for any of the above request-replan.json

Some components have only events and internal interfaces (for example C07), and others may have only an HTTP API. A component folder can be added as soon as one of these files exists.

C01 Web Interface has no folder: it provides no operations, events or internal interfaces of its own. It calls the HTTP APIs of the other components, so each screen follows the openapi.yaml of the component it uses. Sign-in, the bearer token and the acting provider are defined by C02 (c02-identity-access/).

docs.title: OpenAPI rules
docs.text:
• Use OpenAPI 3.1.0.
  • Keep at most one openapi.yaml per component.
  • Tag every operation with the owning component, for example C03 Resource Management.
  • Define paths and schemas in the component file; do not create a committed aggregate file.
  • Include realistic request and response examples where useful.
  • Use clear, stable names for paths, schemas, fields, and versions.
  • Keep breaking changes coordinated with the affected producer and consumers.

The CI workflow automatically discovers all component OpenAPI files, generates a temporary aggregate, validates it, and builds the Redoc site. Component folders without an openapi.yaml are skipped. The generated aggregate is not source code and must not be committed.

docs.title: Local checks
docs.text:
From the repository root:

npm ci
npm run contracts:lint
npm run contracts:build
cd dist && python3 -m http.server 8080

Open http://localhost:8080/ to view the documentation index, or open:

  • http://localhost:8080/openapi/
  • http://localhost:8080/asyncapi/
  • http://localhost:8080/internal/

Install mkdocs-material with python3 -m pip install mkdocs-material before running contracts:build locally.

docs.title: Event rules
docs.text:
Event contracts belong in one events.yaml per component:

  • Use AsyncAPI 3.0.0.
  • Name messages after their event types.
  • Define the channel or exchange, routing key, producer, and payload schema.
  • Include a unique event ID, schema version, correlation ID, entity ID, and entity version where applicable.
  • Include realistic message examples.
  • Consumers must deduplicate messages by event ID.
  • Breaking payload changes require a schema-version change and review by affected consumers.
  • The producer defines the message. A consumer lists the messages it receives with action: receive and refers to the producer's definition rather than copying it.

Event files are validated and rendered as an aggregated AsyncAPI documentation site by the CI workflow.

docs.title: Internal interface rules
docs.text:
The architecture describes component APIs as "logical contracts, not separate public HTTP endpoints for every function", and allows logical components to share a process and database transaction. Those direct calls between components are documented in internal.md:

  • List the interfaces the component provides (other components call them) and the ones it requires (it calls other components).
  • For each provided interface, give the signature, request and response fields (name, type, required, meaning), the Result failure kinds, and any idempotency or ordering rule.
  • A required interface only names the operation, the providing component and how this component uses it. The provider's internal.md is the definition.
  • Link the matching files in examples/.
  • Name the typed model in the code that implements the contract, if there is one.
  • Methods used only inside the component (for example C07 classifyImpact) are not contracts and do not belong here.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
• Put examples in the examples/ folder of the component that owns the contract, so the producer of an event or the provider of an operation.
  • Use kebab-case names that say what the example is: request-replan.json, replan-saved.json, city-state-updated-event.json.
  • Use synthetic data only. Keep shared IDs consistent across examples, so a chain (closure → disruption → replan) can be followed.
  • Backend tests may load these files as fixtures. If you rename or change one, run cd backend && uv run pytest.

docs.title: C02 Identity and Access: internal interfaces
docs.text:
C02 decides who is calling and what they may do. This file covers what other components use inside the backend process. The HTTP boundary for C01 is in openapi.yaml. Implementation: #56 (backend) and #57 (C01 sign-in).

Typed model: planned in backend/app/shared/auth.py (#56). Until then C03 uses its development stand-in in backend/app/integrations/identity.py. Examples: examples/.

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
• C02 owns identity and memberships. Roles and provider memberships come from C02's records, never from the token's custom claims or the request.
  • Requested scope is not permission. A providerId, runId or resource ID in a request is a filter. The component checks it against the AuthContext.
  • Deny by default. An operation with no explicit role check is not exposed.
  • 401 versus 403. No valid token (missing, invalid, expired) is 401 UNAUTHENTICATED. A valid caller without the role or provider is 403 FORBIDDEN. Neither response reveals whether a restricted record exists.
  • Same error format everywhere. {"error": {"code", "message", "correlation_id"}}, as in C03, so C01 needs one error handler.

docs.title: authenticate(request) → Result\<AuthContext>
docs.text:
Callers: every protected HTTP route (as a FastAPI dependency). Examples: examples/auth-context-user.json.

Verifies the bearer token with Supabase Auth, loads the caller's memberships, and resolves the acting provider. A platform admin explicitly selects any existing provider using X-Acting-Provider. An unknown provider or an empty provider directory returns Forbidden. If providers exist, omitting the header returns Invalid. For all other users the following rules apply.

Caller's memberships X-Acting-Provider header Result None any Forbidden (signed in, no access yet) Exactly one absent That provider Exactly one that provider That provider Any a provider they belong to That provider Any a provider they do not belong to Forbidden More than one absent Invalid: the header is required

Failures: Invalid (missing acting provider), Forbidden, and Unavailable (identity provider or records down). A missing or bad token is reported by the route as 401 UNAUTHENTICATED.

AuthContext

Field Type Required Meaning principalId UUID yes Supabase Auth user ID, or the fixed ID of a service principalType enum yes user or service serviceId string service only Component code of a calling service, for example C07 actingProviderId UUID users: yes Provider resolved from the table above; null for services roles array of enum yes The caller's roles in the acting provider (manager, operator, driver, analyst, curator), or ["service"] providerIds array of UUID yes Every provider the caller may select, including all existing providers for a platform admin platformRoles array of enum yes admin, or empty correlationId UUID yes Ties the request to logs, events and decision records

docs.title: service_context(service_id, correlation_id) → AuthContext
docs.text:
Callers: background workers and component-to-component calls that act on their own behalf, for example C07 calling C05 requestReplan. Example: examples/auth-context-service.json.

Returns a service identity (principalType: service, roles: ["service"]). A service context is only created inside the backend, never from an HTTP request.

docs.title: require_role(context, role, provider_id=None) → Result\<None>
docs.text:
Callers: any component operation that needs a role.

The target must match the acting provider. Within it, either the required provider role or the admin platform role grants access.

docs.title: Required interfaces
docs.text: • Supabase Auth: verifies access tokens (signing keys from the project's JWKS endpoint). No other component talks to Supabase Auth directly.

docs.title: Development identities
docs.text: Until #56 lands, C03's stand-in development tokens (dev-manager, dev-operator, dev-other-provider) map onto the same fields: one provider membership each. Tests should build AuthContext values directly rather than use real tokens.

docs.title: Still open
docs.text:
• [ ] Where membership records live: proposed c02_identity_access.provider_memberships (migration in #56).
  • [ ] Session lifetime and refresh behaviour in C01 (#57).
  • [ ] JSON field style: C02 and C03 errors use correlation_id (snake_case); C06, C11 and C12 bodies use camelCase. Agree one style for new contracts.

docs.title: C04 Delivery Management: internal interfaces
docs.text: C04 validates and owns delivery requests, their constraints, and authoritative progress. A stored request is not a feasible plan, an allocation, or a dispatch instruction. HTTP operations are defined in openapi.yaml, and outbound messages are defined in events.yaml.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text: Use camelCase JSON, UUID v4 identifiers, positive integer versions, and UTC RFC 3339 timestamps. Mutating operations use an idempotency key and expected versions. State changes and their outbox entries commit atomically. Consumers deduplicate by event ID and reject stale delivery versions.

docs.title: Shared parameters: AuthContext and RunScopeSelector
docs.text:
• AuthContext is owned by C02 (see C02 internal.md). A caller-supplied provider ID, delivery ID, or runId is a selector, never permission; C04 checks every call against context.
  • RunScopeSelector follows the shared RunScope contract in backend/app/shared/contracts.py (EventMetadata) and C12 internal.md:
Field Type Required Meaning scope enum (live, simulation) yes Distinguishes live operations from an isolated simulation run runId UUID or null conditional Required UUID v4 when scope is simulation; must be null/absent when scope is live

docs.title: Run-scope isolation rules
docs.text:
1. Strict validation: Passing scope: "live" with a non-null runId, or passing scope: "simulation" without a valid UUID v4 runId, fails immediately with Invalid (C04.INVALID_RUN_SCOPE). An unspecified simulation run is never silently treated as live.
  2. Authorisation: C04 verifies with C02 that context is authorised for the requested runScope (including the specific runId for simulation calls). Unauthorised callers receive Forbidden without revealing whether records exist.
  3. Partitioned storage, idempotency, and versions: Every delivery request is permanently bound to the (scope, runId) in which it was created. Reads, mutations, expected-version checks, idempotency keys, and outbox events are strictly partitioned by (scope, runId). Emitted events carry the same scope and runId in their EventEnvelope.
  4. Cross-run and cross-scope rejection: If any deliveryId passed to getRequests, markRequestsPlanned, or updateProgress belongs to a different runId or to the opposite scope (live vs simulation), C04 rejects the entire call with NotFound (C04.DELIVERY_NOT_FOUND) and commits no changes (no partial links, no progress updates, no outbox entries). Returning NotFound avoids leaking whether an entity exists in another run or in live state.
  5. Isolated simulation writers vs. C12 replay: Isolated simulation services (for example C05 planning or simulated status adapters running inside a simulation run) may call getRequests, markRequestsPlanned, and updateProgress with scope: "simulation" and their authorised runId. C12 replay playback is strictly read-only over saved simulation outcomes and C10 saved evidence; replay must never call markRequestsPlanned, updateProgress, or any mutating C04 operation, and must never read or change live requests.

Examples: simulation getRequests and cross-run failure.

docs.title: getRequests(context, runScope, requestIds) → Result\<DeliveryRequest[]>
docs.text:
C05 reads the authoritative request facts before generating or revising a plan (including UC07 replanning). The response includes the current version and progress, but never a selected vehicle, route, allocation, or execution guarantee.

Field Type Required Meaning context AuthContext yes Caller identity, roles, provider scope, and correlation ID runScope RunScopeSelector yes Target scope (live or simulation) and conditional runId requestIds array of UUID yes Delivery requests to read; must contain at least one ID

Each returned DeliveryRequest contains the fields in the C04Delivery schema, including deliveryId, version, pickup, destination, cargo, timeWindow, constraints (vehicleKinds: van, truck, cargo_bike), status, and progress.

Failures: Invalid (including C04.INVALID_RUN_SCOPE), Forbidden, NotFound (C04.DELIVERY_NOT_FOUND when any requested ID does not exist in the given runScope, including cross-run or live/simulation mismatches), Unavailable.

docs.title: markRequestsPlanned(context, runScope, requestIds, planId, expectedVersions, key) → Result\<Receipt>
docs.text:
C05 calls this operation in the same logical confirmation transaction as its plan state and PlanReady outbox entry. It links requests to a saved plan within the given runScope; it does not allocate resources or mark deliveries as in progress.

Field Type Required Meaning context AuthContext yes Authorised C05 service identity runScope RunScopeSelector yes Target scope (live or simulation) and conditional runId requestIds array of UUID yes Requests included in the confirmed plan planId UUID yes C05 plan that owns the link expectedVersions map UUID → integer yes Version checked for every request key string yes Idempotency key scoped to caller, operation, and runScope

Response: Receipt

Field Type Required Meaning requestIds array of UUID yes Requests linked by this receipt planId UUID yes Confirmed plan reference versions map UUID → integer yes Versions after the link

Failures: Invalid (C04.INVALID_RUN_SCOPE or malformed fields), Forbidden, NotFound (C04.DELIVERY_NOT_FOUND if any request is missing or belongs to another runScope; no partial links are committed), Conflict, Unavailable. Conflict means a request version or status changed; no partial links are committed. Retrying the same scoped key and request returns the first receipt.

docs.title: updateProgress(context, runScope, deliveryId, progress, key) → Result\<DeliveryRequest>
docs.text:
The authorised provider/status adapter (or isolated simulation status adapter) uses this operation to record actual progress within runScope. It emits DeliveryProgressChanged with the same scope and runId; it does not change planning or allocation state.

Field Type Required Meaning context AuthContext yes Authorised provider or simulation status adapter identity runScope RunScopeSelector yes Target scope (live or simulation) and conditional runId deliveryId UUID yes Delivery whose progress changed progress C04Progress yes Authoritative progress status and business occurrence time (updatedAt) key string yes Idempotency key scoped to caller, operation, and runScope

progress.updatedAt is the actual business occurrence time (UTC RFC 3339) when the progress transition happened (e.g., actual delivery time when status == "delivered"), not database commit time or event emittedAt.

Failures: Invalid (C04.INVALID_RUN_SCOPE or invalid transition), Forbidden, NotFound (C04.DELIVERY_NOT_FOUND if missing or in another runScope; no changes committed), Conflict, Unavailable.

docs.title: Required interfaces
docs.text:
Provider Operation Use by C04 C02 authorize(context, action, scope) Authorise submit, read, update, and provider progress operations (see C02 internal.md) Mapping adapter validateLocations(pickup, destination) Confirm both locations before storing a request C10 recordOutcome(conn, ctx, outcome) → Result<AuditId> Record the result of protected commands and progress changes (see C10 internal.md)

The provider owns the definitions of these required operations; C04 does not copy their schemas here.

docs.title: C10 outcome recording
docs.text:
C04 invokes C10's recordOutcome(conn, ctx, outcome) → Result<AuditId> in-process following C10 internal.md:

  • Transactional behaviour: For committed mutations, recordOutcome runs inside C04's database transaction on the caller's conn and never commits on its own (if C04 rolls back, the audit record rolls back too). Rejected operations (Invalid, Forbidden, NotFound, Conflict, Unavailable) are recorded in their own short transaction.
  • Context propagation: principalId and correlationId are taken from ctx (AuthContext).
  • Operation naming: outcome.operation uses the C04.<operation> format.
  • Recorded C04 operations:
  • C04.submitDeliveryRequest (HTTP POST /api/v1/deliveries)
  • C04.updateDeliveryRequest (HTTP POST /api/v1/deliveries/{deliveryId})
  • C04.markRequestsPlanned (internal plan confirmation link from C05)
  • C04.updateProgress (internal progress update from provider/simulation adapter)

docs.title: Ownership and ordering
docs.text:
• C04 owns request identity, locations, cargo, constraints, request status, and progress. C05 owns plan state; C08 owns allocation and execution commitments.
  • pending requests may be edited. Once linked to a confirmed plan, request facts are immutable through the update operation.
  • A retry with the same caller, runScope, operation, key, and body returns the original committed result. Reusing a key with a different body returns Conflict.
  • Events retain their eventId on transport retry. Consumers use entityVersions[deliveryId] and deliveryVersion to ignore stale updates.

docs.title: C05 Planning and Replanning
docs.text:
Contract draft for UC03 and UC07, issue #32. Pair Ye + Zecheng. Reviewers Bruno or Alejandro for C07 compatibility. Proposed HTTP and event fields require review with C01, C08 and C10 before implementation.

C05 owns proposals, confirmed plans and revisions. C08 owns actual allocation and operational commitments. Planning reads those facts when checking feasibility.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
Use camelCase JSON, UUID v4 identifiers, positive integer versions and UTC RFC 3339 timestamps. Reuse the shared Result<T> from backend/app/shared/result.py. A successful internal call returns Ok(value); a failure returns Failure(kind, message). JSON examples show the success value. The existing PlanningPort returns unwrapped values and raises PlanningUnavailableError for unavailability. Its future C05 adapter must map these to and from the logical Result contract.

The adopted C07 models remain in backend/app/components/c07_disruption_detection/contracts.py for compatibility. ChangeScope, AffectedWork, ReplanRequest and ReplanOutcome are the current typed models. PlanningPort in the adjacent planning.py is the current caller interface. This documentation migration preserves their fields and imports.

docs.title: findAffectedWork(changeScope) → Result\<AffectedWork>
docs.text:
C07 asks C05 which unfinished work a change touches. C05 owns plans, so it decides what "affected" means for a route; C07 only says where and what changed. For the slice, C07 sends one call per changed segment.

Examples request and response.

Request: changeScope

Field Type Required Meaning segmentKeys array of string one of Segments whose condition changed resourceIds array of UUID one of Resources whose availability changed or failed planIds array of UUID one of Plans named directly (for example by OperationalDisruption) from / to timestamp no Time window the change applies to; default now → open-ended

Response: AffectedWork

Field Type Required Meaning items array yes Empty when nothing is affected items[].planId UUID yes Plan touching the scope items[].planVersion integer yes Current version C05 checked against items[].deliveryIds array of UUID yes Unfinished deliveries on the affected part; completed ones excluded items[].matchedSegmentKeys array of string no Which of the requested segments the route uses items[].matchedResourceIds array of UUID no Which requested resources the plan relies on

Failures: Invalid, Unavailable (C07 then reports disruption status unknown).

docs.title: requestReplan(context, planId, trigger, key) → Result\<ReplanOutcome>
docs.text:
C07 sends one requestReplan per affected plan. The call is synchronous: C05 answers with a final outcome straight away.

Examples request, saved outcome and conflict failure.

Request

Field Type Required Meaning context AuthContext yes Service identity C07, plus correlationId planId UUID yes Plan to revise trigger.disruptionId UUID yes Disruption record behind the request trigger.disruptionVersion integer yes Version of that record trigger.basedOnPlanVersion integer yes Plan version returned by findAffectedWork trigger.reason enum yes road_closed / congestion / resource_unavailable / operational_failure / weather trigger.citySnapshotVersion integer no Snapshot the disruption was judged on trigger.sourceEventId UUID yes Event that started the chain key string yes Idempotency key = planId:disruptionId:disruptionVersion

Response: ReplanOutcome

Field Type Required Meaning status enum yes NoChange / ReviewRequired / PlanSaved newPlanVersion integer when saved Version of the saved revision decisionId UUID when saved C10 decision record

The inherited logical draft lists Conflict, Infeasible, Unavailable and NotFound. The current PlanningPort returns an unwrapped ReplanOutcome or raises PlanningUnavailableError. C07 catches that exception and otherwise records outcome.status. Agree the mapping of other logical failures and any Conflict discovery retry with C07 before connecting the C05 adapter.

The idempotency key is what stops the C08 → C07 → C05 loop. The same disruption version can never produce a second replan of the same plan; C05 returns the first outcome again.

docs.title: Required interfaces
docs.text:
Provider Operation Use by C05 C02 authorize(context, action, scope) Authorise generation, confirmation and reads within the permitted scope C03 listEligibleResources(scope) Read resource capabilities, observed availability and quality C04 getRequests(context, requestIds) Read requirements, versions and progress C04 markRequestsPlanned(requestIds, planId) Link deliveries when confirming a plan C06 getCitySnapshot(scope, freshnessPolicy) Read versioned and quality-labelled city conditions; definition in C06 C09 queryKnowledge(context, policyQuery) Obtain applicable policy evidence and provenance C10 recordDecision(decisionRecord) Preserve actual input versions, alternatives, reasons and exact evidence used

C02/C03/C04/C09/C10 provider definitions remain authoritative as their contracts are published. Required operations listed here do not define their fields.

docs.title: Planning and persistence rules
docs.text:
The proposed C01 HTTP operations are in openapi.yaml. Authentication is obtained from the bearer token. HTTP paths use /api/v1/plans; HTTP errors use the C11/C12-style error { code, message, correlationId } envelope proposal, pending shared frontend review. This transport mapping does not change the internal Result contract or C07 models. Authorisation and scope checks use C02. An initial proposal awaits operator confirmation. Confirmation checks its expected version, links its deliveries and queues PlanReady atomically with the confirmed state and decision references. A saved revision atomically records its expected-version update, C10-owned decision/evidence and PlanReady outbox entry.

C10 evidence contains the exact passages and source/version/provenance used at decision time. Evidence is retained after the C09 corpus changes. An outbox publisher retries the saved event ID without rerunning planning. Failure to commit any authoritative state, evidence or outbox entry rolls back the operation.

For UC07, trigger.citySnapshotVersion records the City State that triggered the request when C07 provides it. C05 reads current conditions in the same run and records the version it actually uses for the decision.

C08 uses planId, planVersion and the event's run scope to look up C05's current plan. It rechecks that the event version is still current before committing resources. The requirements list describes all resource needs for unfinished deliveries in that plan version. C08 checks which existing commitments still satisfy those needs against the revised route and timing.

For mutating HTTP calls, a retry with the same caller, operation, run scope, key and request returns the first committed response. Reusing that key with a different request gives Conflict. Concurrent writes use expected-version checks. A lost response after commit is recovered by retrying the same request and key.

docs.title: Example sequence
docs.text: The proposal at version 2 is confirmed with expectedVersion 2, giving the confirmed plan at version 3. The earlier version 1 is outside this excerpt. After C06 records snapshot 42, C07 requests a replan based on version 3. The saved outcome refers to revision 4, which avoids seg:4471023. Versions 3 and 4 have the same van capacity requirement. The PlanReady event carries that requirement with version 4 and its decision ID. It retains the closure correlation ID and simulation run ID and has its own event ID. HTTP examples and this event illustrate proposed fields pending consumer review.

docs.title: Open coordination points
docs.text:
• The HTTP paths, proposal representation, priorities and resource-needs schema are proposals for C01/C03/C04/C08 review. Only the two C07 interfaces above have existing typed models. New HTTP/event schemas have no runtime yet.
  • The existing PlanningPort passes no run scope or run ID to either method. Agree scope propagation with C07 before connecting simulation to real C05 storage. A simulation must resolve only its run's plans, inputs and receipts. Do not silently treat an unspecified simulation run as live.
  • Agree with C07 whether one fresh discovery is allowed after a stale-plan Conflict, and whether that conflict consumes the key. A refreshed basedOnPlanVersion changes the request but leaves the current key unchanged.
  • The inherited logical draft lists Infeasible, while architecture UC07 returns ReviewRequired for an infeasible revision. Agree that mapping with C07. The current ReplanOutcome has no reason/details field.
  • Agree with C07 when the synchronous PlanSaved outcome is returned and how to report a saved revision while PlanReady publication is pending. PlanReady is the event for confirmation and saved revisions.
  • Exchange/routing and the canonical shared event envelope are tracked in #28. The event draft refers to the existing C06 envelope to avoid another copy.
  • C05 receives replanning through an internal call from C07. No direct subscription to CityStateUpdated is currently proposed.

docs.title: C06 City Monitoring: internal interfaces
docs.text:
C06 owns City State (UC05). This file covers the calls other components make to C06 inside the backend process. Events are in events.yaml. HTTP operations for C01 and other clients are in openapi.yaml (getCitySnapshot so far; submitManualCondition will follow).

Typed models: backend/app/components/c06_city_monitoring/contracts.py and backend/app/shared/contracts.py. Examples: examples/.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
These conventions apply to the C06 and C07 contracts. All pairs need to agree them once (#28).

Item Convention Identifiers UUID v4 strings for every entity and event ID (eventId, planId, disruptionId, ...) Versions Integers starting at 1, incremented on every committed change to an entity Timestamps ISO 8601 in UTC with Z suffix, for example 2026-11-20T08:15:00Z; the UI converts to local time Road segment key seg:<osm_way_id> (OpenStreetMap way ID), for example seg:4471023. Agreed. Zone key zone:<code>, using a fixed grid or Dublin postal district (to decide) Units Speed in km/h, delay in seconds, rainfall in mm/h, temperature in °C, distance in metres Quality Enum good / degraded / unknown on any observed or derived value Run scope live or simulation, plus runId when simulation; replay never writes to live Failure outcomes The shared Result<T> kinds: Invalid, Forbidden, NotFound, Conflict, Unavailable, Unconfirmed, Infeasible, Partial

Where a field is marked slice: no, it can be left out until Iteration 3 but the name is reserved.

docs.title: getCitySnapshot(scope, freshnessPolicy) → Result\<CitySnapshot>
docs.text:
Callers: C05 (planning) and C07 (full context after CityStateUpdated). Examples: examples/city-snapshot-query.json, examples/city-snapshot.json.

Request: CitySnapshotQuery

Field Type Required Meaning scope.segmentKeys array of string one of Specific segments scope.bbox [minLon, minLat, maxLon, maxLat] one of Area query freshnessPolicy.maxAgeSeconds integer no Values older than this come back degraded; default 900 atVersion integer no Read a past snapshot version (used by C10/C12)

Response: CitySnapshot

Field Type Required Meaning snapshotVersion integer yes Monotonic City State version generatedAt timestamp yes When this snapshot was assembled segments array of SegmentCondition yes Only segments with a non-default condition; absent = open, good staleSources array of string yes Empty when all feeds are fresh overallQuality enum yes Worst quality among returned values

SegmentCondition is defined in events.yaml (components.schemas.SegmentCondition).

Behaviour (implemented in backend/app/components/c06_city_monitoring/snapshot.py):

  • The caller also passes the City State scope: live, or one simulation runId. A run's state is never mixed with live state.
  • Requested segments without a recorded condition are omitted (absent means open, good).
  • In a current snapshot, a good value older than maxAgeSeconds (default 900) is returned as degraded and its sources are listed in staleSources. Past versions (atVersion) are returned as they were recorded.
  • overallQuality is the worst quality among the returned segments, or good when none are returned.
  • scope.bbox is rejected as Invalid until segments have geometry in C06.
  • scope.segmentKeys must hold 1 to 200 keys, the same limit as openapi.yaml.
  • A read has no side effects: it sees committed City State and never writes, so an ingestion committed during the read is kept. Returned segments are copies.

Failures: Invalid (bad scope, bbox, or 0 or more than 200 segment keys), NotFound (atVersion newer than the current version), Unavailable (no City State yet, or store down), Forbidden.

docs.title: ingestObservation(sourceContext, observation) → Result\<IngestionReceipt>
docs.text:
Callers: the traffic, weather and event source adapters, and manual reports. Examples: examples/observation-closure.json, examples/ingestion-receipt.json.

Request: Observation

Field Type Required Meaning observationId UUID yes Assigned by source or C06; dedup key sourceId string yes For example sim-traffic, manual kind enum yes traffic / weather / event / closure target object yes { "segmentKey" } or { "zoneKey" } or { "lat", "lon" } (C06 maps to a segment) values object yes Raw values in source units, for example { "status": "closed" } observedAt timestamp yes Source time; older than current → history only (AF4) author / expiresAt string / timestamp manual only AF5

Response: IngestionReceipt

Field Type Required Meaning observationId UUID yes The ingested observation disposition enum yes merged / history_only / conflict / rejected snapshotVersion integer when merged New City State version

Re-ingesting the same observationId returns the first receipt and changes nothing. A merged observation commits the City State change and the CityStateUpdated outbox entry in one transaction.

Failures: Invalid (unusable values or unsupported target), Unavailable (store down; nothing is saved).

Zone-level weather (zoneKey, rainMmH, tempC, windKmh, quality) follows the same pattern. slice: no.

docs.title: Required interfaces
docs.text: None yet. Source authentication will use C02 once its contract exists.

  • [ ] Zones: fixed grid or postal districts? Only needed for weather, so this can wait.

docs.title: C07 Disruption Detection: internal interfaces
docs.text:
C07 evaluates disruptions (UC06) and requests separate replanning. It has no HTTP operations. The events it consumes are in events.yaml, and its evaluateChange handler is triggered by them. This file covers the calls C07 makes to other components and the record it owns.

Typed models: backend/app/components/c07_disruption_detection/contracts.py. Conventions (IDs, versions, timestamps, quality, run scope, Result failures): see ../c06-city-monitoring/internal.md.

docs.title: Provided interfaces
docs.text: None. Other components learn about disruptions through the replan requests C07 sends to C05.

docs.title: Owned record: Disruption
docs.text:
C10 and C12 will read it, so it should stay stable. Persisted by upsertDisruption. Example: examples/disruption.json.

Field Type Required Meaning disruptionId UUID yes Stable across updates version integer yes Bumped only on a material change: status or severity changes, or a new affected plan status enum yes active / resolved / unknown cause enum yes Same as SegmentCondition cause, plus resource / operational severity enum yes low / medium / high. Slice rule: closed on a used segment = high segmentKeys / resourceIds arrays yes What is disrupted affectedPlans array yes [{ planId, planVersion, replanRequested, replanOutcome }] triggerEventIds array of UUID yes Every event folded into this record (dedup) quality enum yes Confidence in the classification createdAt / updatedAt timestamp yes

docs.title: C05 planning operations
docs.text: C07 requires findAffectedWork(changeScope) and the synchronous, idempotent requestReplan(context, planId, trigger, key). C05 owns their definitions and examples in C05 internal interfaces. C07 uses the returned plan versions and final outcomes to update its disruption record. The proposed discovery retry on a version conflict is listed in the C05 coordination points.

docs.title: C06 getCitySnapshot(scope, freshnessPolicy) → Result\<CitySnapshot>
docs.text: Defined in ../c06-city-monitoring/internal.md. C07 uses it when a CityStateUpdated event does not carry enough context. Not used by the thin slice.

docs.title: Decisions (16 Nov 2026)
docs.text:
• [x] Segment keys: seg:<osm_way_id> (OpenStreetMap way ID).
  • [x] Default maxAgeSeconds for freshness: 900 s.
  • [x] Material change that bumps a disruption version: status or severity changes, or new affected plans.
  • [x] Severity rule for the slice: closed on a used segment = high; anything else is out of scope until Iteration 3.
  • [x] findAffectedWork: one C05 call per changed segment for now.
  • [x] requestReplan is synchronous; PublicationPending is dropped from ReplanOutcome.

docs.title: C08 Allocation and Resource Agents
docs.text: Contract draft for UC04 and UC08. Óscar Gómez González and Shixian Cai own the C08 implementation. Python models and the C08 service protocol live in backend/app/components/c08_allocation/.

docs.title: HTTP boundary
docs.text: The UC04 OpenAPI contract defines the operator's assignment request and the driver's offer response. The HTTP adapter derives identity from authentication and passes the idempotency key to the service. Assignment finalisation and UC08 negotiation are internal C08 operations.

docs.title: Event boundaries
docs.text:
• C05 emits PlanReady after operator confirmation in UC03 and after the revised plan commits in UC07. The version and its outbox intent are saved together. Each event includes the full set of resource requirements for unfinished deliveries in that version. The single affected plan and its entity version must agree with the payload. C05 owns the producer contract.
  • The C05 confirmed simulation v3 and route-only revision event v4 share a plan and run ID. The route and schedule are read from the saved C05 version for that run. The requirements stay the same; C08 reuses commitments that still fit the revised route and schedule and checks that the plan version is current before committing resources.
  • ResourceAvailabilityChanged uses C03's producer contract. UC04 checks whether the change affects the vehicle selected for a pending assignment. See the C03 availability example. The C03 producer currently has a component-specific envelope. C03 owns the change to the shared envelope.
  • OperationalDisruption example. C08 sends the actual committed state and the unresolved delivery IDs. C07 uses failureId as the stable trigger identity. Broker redelivery reuses eventId; it does not start a second negotiation or replan.

docs.title: C08 provides
docs.text:
Operation Input Result and lifecycle handle_plan_ready PlanReadyEvent AllocationOutcome. Deduplicate the event, skip superseded versions, and reuse valid commitments. negotiate_allocation AuthContext, AllocationProblem, command key AllocationOutcome. Run one bounded proposal round. UC08 agent receipts are independent of driver acceptance. commit_negotiation CommitNegotiationCommand with proposal and expected plan/resource versions AllocationOutcome. Commit capacity and report the selected resource, assignment reference and resulting versions. assign_vehicle AssignVehicleCommand with plan, delivery, expected version and key AllocationOutcome. Reuse the UC08 reference when available, or reserve a candidate for an offer. record_offer_response OfferResponseCommand with offer, response and key AllocationOutcome. Record the driver's acceptance or rejection in UC04. commit_assignment CommitAssignmentCommand with assignment reference, expected plan version and key AllocationOutcome. Recheck versions, eligibility and capacity, then finalise the accepted reference without consuming capacity again. publish_operational_disruption AuthContext, OperationalDisruptionPayload, command key Event UUID. Persist the failure and outbox intent together. C07 evaluates any separate replan.

Mutations replay the prior result for the same command and key. A reused key with a different command payload returns a conflict. Allocation commands can return conflict, forbidden, invalid or unavailable outcomes, plus the relevant workflow status defined by OutcomeCode. Commit authoritative state, C10 decision evidence and outbox intent in one short PostgreSQL transaction. Publish after commit. Executable driver instructions require accepted and committed UC04 assignment state.

docs.title: Required interfaces and review points
docs.text:
• C05 supplies the saved plan version and resource needs. Review the PlanReady fixture and the authoritative plan-version lookup at commit.
  • C03 owns resource profiles, observed availability and resource versions. C08 owns reserved and committed capacity. Agree the capacity dimensions, numeric precision, and resource-version checks before writing migrations.
  • C10 supplies the decision/evidence write contract. Preserve the exact decision-time content and source versions in the authoritative transaction.
  • C01 and C08 agree driver identity, offers, expiry and responses. Confirm how the assignment reference binds the resource version used at finalisation.

docs.title: C09 Logistics Knowledge: internal interfaces
docs.text:
C09 owns the curated policy corpus and knowledge retrieval (UC09). The HTTP operations used by the browser (C01: curator publishing, operator lookups) are in openapi.yaml. This file covers the calls other components make inside the backend process.

Typed models: backend/app/components/c09_logistics_knowledge/contracts.py; service: backend/app/components/c09_logistics_knowledge/service.py. Conventions and AuthContext: see ../c10-decision-records/internal.md. Draft v0.1, owned by Qingyuan + Bangchen (#13).

docs.title: queryKnowledge(ctx, query: PolicyQuery) → Result\<KnowledgeResult>
docs.text:
Called by C05 before generating or replanning a plan, and by C08 when evaluating agent proposals. It is the same operation as HTTP POST /api/c09/knowledge/query; request and response are the C09PolicyQuery and C09KnowledgeResult schemas in openapi.yaml, with its examples.

  • Read-only; no idempotency key. Roles: Service:C05, Service:C08.
  • Returns applicable passages of the active corpus, ranked by similarity to freeText (all score 1.0 without it).
  • Every applicable passage that carries constraints is always returned and checked for conflicts; maxPassages only limits rule-free passages. ruleCoverage: Incomplete (explained in limitations) means not all hard rules could be returned: UC03 returns DataUnavailable and UC07 ReviewRequired without saving a revision. C10 rejects a Selected decision built on it.
  • Rule scope: a constraint applies inside its zoneIds; when segmentKeys is non-empty, only on those C06 segments. C05 matches them against the route and stop segments, so a detour off those segments is not bound by the rule. Required fields per kind: VehicleBan value null; LoadingWindow needs timeOfDay, value null; MaxGrossWeight needs value: {"maxKg": >0}.
  • Provenance (corpusVersion, indexVersion, embeddingModel, retrievedAt, ruleCoverage, conflicts, limitations) is repeated on the result for convenience; it must equal the evidenceSnapshot, which is the record.
  • Same request on the same corpusVersion gives the same order.
  • status: Ok, LowConfidence, Conflict or NoApplicable. None of these is a failure; record limitations in the decision.
  • Pass evidenceSnapshot unchanged to C10 recordDecision.
  • Callers time out after 5 s and treat that as Unavailable.

Failures: Invalid (C09.INVALID_TIME_WINDOW, C09.UNKNOWN_ZONE), Forbidden (C09.FORBIDDEN), Unavailable (C09.INDEX_UNAVAILABLE, C09.EMBEDDING_UNAVAILABLE): plan with hard constraints only and record the limitation knowledge unavailable.

docs.title: Required interfaces
docs.text: None. Curator conflict warnings (notifyKnowledgeConflict) are used only inside C09 and are not a contract.

docs.title: C10 Decision Records and Explanation: internal interfaces
docs.text:
C10 stores decision-time evidence and explains saved decisions (UC10). The HTTP operations used by the browser (C01) are in openapi.yaml. This file covers the calls other components make inside the backend process.

Typed models: backend/app/components/c10_decision_records/contracts.py, shared types in backend/app/shared/c09_c10_common.py. Draft v0.1, owned by Qingyuan + Bangchen (#13).

Conventions: JSON is camelCase, timestamps are UTC ISO 8601 with Z, IDs are UUID v4, unknown fields are rejected. Every call returns Result<T>: Ok or a failure kind Invalid, Forbidden, NotFound, Conflict, Unavailable, with a C10.* code.

docs.title: Shared parameter: AuthContext
docs.text:
Built by the caller from the authenticated request; IDs alone never grant access.

Field Type Required Meaning principalId string yes User ID or service:<name> principalType enum yes User / Service roles array of string yes e.g. Service:C05, LogisticsOperator, Analyst scope object no {providerIds?, zoneIds?}; absent means no provider/zone limit correlationId UUID yes Carried through one user operation

docs.title: recordDecision(conn, ctx, record: DecisionRecord) → Result\<RecordDecisionResponse>
docs.text:
Called by C05 (plans, replans) and C08 (allocations, negotiations) when they save a decision. It runs inside the caller's database transaction on the caller's connection and never commits: if the caller rolls back, the decision and its evidence are rolled back too. Records are insert-only.

Examples: examples/record-decision-request.json (plan selected), examples/record-decision-data-unavailable-request.json (failed UC03 attempt, no plan yet), examples/record-decision-response.json.

C05 owns the commit or rollback. For UC07 the revision, the decision record and the PlanReady outbox entry commit together.

Request: DecisionRecord

Field Type Required Meaning decisionId UUID yes Generated by the caller idempotencyKey string yes Suggested <producer>:<subjectType>:<id>:v<version>; without a version <producer>:PlanningAttempt:<attemptId> decisionType enum yes PlanGenerated / Replan / Allocation / Negotiation producer enum yes C05 / C08; must match the calling service decidedBy string yes Principal (agent or user) that decided subject object yes {type, id, version}; type = Plan / Allocation / Negotiation / PlanningAttempt. version is null when no saved version exists (always for PlanningAttempt) attemptOutcome enum yes Selected / Infeasible / DataUnavailable (UC03) / NoChange / ReviewRequired (UC07) relatedDecisionId UUID or null yes Previous decision; required for Replan inputVersions object yes {deliveries[{id,version}], resources[{id,version}], citySnapshotVersion, corpusVersion} actually used selectedOption object or null yes {optionId, summary, details}; required for Selected, null otherwise. Never invented for a failed attempt consideredAlternatives array yes Only options really considered: {optionId, summary, metrics?, rejectedReason, evidenceRefIds[]} reasons array (≥1) yes {reasonId, text, evidenceRefIds[]} predictedEffects object no {etaMin?, distanceKm?, costEur?, co2Kg?}, estimates evidenceSnapshots array yes C09 EvidenceSnapshots passed through unchanged; may be empty with a limitation limitations array of string yes E.g. knowledge unavailable runScope object yes {mode: Live/Simulation, runId}; runId required for Simulation decidedAt timestamp yes

Rules checked by the model:

  • Every evidenceRefIds entry must be a passageId inside evidenceSnapshots.
  • A Selected decision has a selectedOption and a saved subject.version; other outcomes have neither option nor invented version.
  • One corpus version per decision: all evidenceSnapshots share inputVersions.corpusVersion (null when no knowledge was used). If the corpus changes between C05's queries, C05 re-queries before deciding.
  • No Selected decision on a snapshot with ruleCoverage: Incomplete.

Response: RecordDecisionResponse

Field Type Required Meaning decisionId UUID yes Original ID, also on a duplicate recordedAt timestamp yes duplicate boolean yes true when the same key and body were recorded before

Failures

Kind Code When Caller action Invalid C10.MISSING_FIELD Missing field or bad enum Fix the record Invalid C10.EVIDENCE_REF_MISSING A reason/alternative cites a refId not in the snapshots Fix the record Invalid C10.EVIDENCE_CONTENT_MISSING A snapshot item has no content Pass C09's snapshot unchanged Forbidden C10.PRODUCER_MISMATCH producer differs from the calling service Conflict C10.IDEMPOTENCY_MISMATCH Same key, different body Roll back

docs.title: recordOutcome(conn, ctx, outcome: AuditOutcome) → Result\<AuditId>
docs.text:
Called by every component for each protected write, including rejected ones. Runs in the caller's transaction; a rejected operation is recorded in its own short transaction. principalId and correlationId come from ctx.

Examples: examples/record-outcome-request.json, examples/record-outcome-response.json.

Field Type Required Meaning operation string yes <Component>.<operation>, e.g. C04.submitDeliveryRequest outcome enum yes Ok, Invalid, Forbidden, NotFound, Conflict, Unavailable, Infeasible, Partial, Unconfirmed targetIds array of string yes Affected entity IDs; may be empty occurredAt timestamp yes details object no Never secrets, tokens or unnecessary personal data

Response AuditId: {auditId: UUID}.

docs.title: Run-scoped explanation for C12 replay (UC12)
docs.text:
C12 calls the same operations as the HTTP API in openapi.yaml, in process: getDecision, getDecisionEvidence and explainDecision, with the same request and response models. During replay C12 must pass its runId with the decisionId (DecisionIdSelector {decisionId, runId}); C10 answers NotFound (C10.DECISION_NOT_FOUND) unless the decision was recorded in that run, so a replay can never read another run's decisions. Explanations use only evidence saved at decision time; C10 never queries today's C09 corpus.

Example: openapi.yaml → components.examples.C10ExplainDecisionReplayRequest.

docs.title: Required interfaces
docs.text: None. C10 does not call other components; explanation text comes from an external language-model API, with a structured fallback when it is unavailable.

docs.title: C11 KPI Analytics: internal interfaces (UC11)
docs.text:
Status: contract proposal; no runtime endpoint is implemented here. Follows #35/#46; HTTP publication is tracked by #48. Pair: Jolin + Qingyuan. Requested HTTP reviewers: Julian (Antel0p3) and Oscar (OscarGomezGonzalezz). AI-assisted preparation for Jolin; no completed paired work or UC12 handover is claimed.

The C01-facing API definitions, field schemas, examples and HTTP failures now live in openapi.yaml. Browser calls are not internal interfaces. Transport proposals (paths, paging, idempotency receipts and error envelopes) need consumer review. In-process Result<T>, C02 context and typed models remain unchanged; HTTP adapters translate them rather than redefining shared types. Event contracts stay in events.yaml.

docs.title: C01 HTTP operations
docs.text:
Logical operation HTTP contract queryKPIs POST /api/v1/analytics/kpis/query getKPIBreakdown POST /api/v1/analytics/kpis/{metricId}/breakdown

Schemas and request/response/error definitions belong only to openapi.yaml. Existing value models remain in backend/app/components/c11_kpi_analytics/contracts.py.

docs.title:
consumeOperationalEvent(event) → Result

Callers: trusted operational-event adapters for C04/C05/C06/C08, with C10 outcome/record access to be agreed. Input is the producer-owned EventEnvelope: eventId, eventType, schemaVersion, producer, observedAt, emittedAt, correlationId, affected, scope, payload, plus optional causationId, entityVersions and simulation runId. See C06's shared envelope definition. Check producer identity, event type/version and authorised scope before processing.

Atomically deduplicate eventId with the read-model update, preserve source/coverage provenance and return the same receipt on redelivery. Never send an operational command. Receipt fields and the producer subscription set remain unagreed; this format migration does not fabricate a DTO or declare subscriptions to events whose owners have not published contracts. events.yaml references the existing C06 definition as a proposed input, not an agreed metric formula.

Failures: Invalid (unsupported envelope/payload/version), Forbidden (untrusted producer/scope), Conflict (incompatible duplicate), Unavailable (read-model/receipt store; no partial commit). Transient delivery retry policy remains an infrastructure agreement.
Result semantics and unresolved metric definitions
docs.text:
• Missing: null value, unavailable status and explicit reason, never zero.
  • A measured zero is valid only with observations. Usable indicators need a value and lastUpdated; no observations cannot produce a value.
  • observed cannot exceed eligible. available requires observed == eligible; incomplete coverage is partial. Excluded records are counted separately.
  • Estimates require versioned estimationBasis and are never labelled measured.
  • Trends use period-specific indicators with matching units/definition versions.
  • A refresh failure retains previous values and original lastUpdated, returns status: stale and failure. Without previous results return Unavailable; generatedAt is response time. Current sets cannot contain partial/missing items.
  • Initial families: delivery time, cost, congestion and environmental impact. Formulas, weights, rates, factors, denominators, freshness thresholds and exact source payloads are not approved. fixture-v1-not-approved, seconds/EUR and synthetic supporting records illustrate shape, not production calculation.

docs.title: Required interfaces and agreements
docs.text:
Provider Required contract/use Status C02 Authenticated principal, roles, provider/area/resource authorisation. Owning pair defines it; no local replacement AuthContext. C04/C05/C08 Authoritative delivery, plan, movement and allocation outcomes used for populations and metrics. Owners must publish payloads/units/versions; no copied definitions here. C06 City/observation data for congestion and affected-area semantics. Refer to C06 internal interfaces and its event definition; metric input selection pending. C10 Operational outcome/record access and audit integration if needed. Owning pair must define access and retention. C01 / consumers Metric configuration/version, breakdown paging and view adapter. Agree before runtime implementation.

Only the provider defines a required operation. No producer schema or internal component helper is redefined here. This proposal changes no other component.

docs.title: Persistence, verification and follow-up
docs.text:
No database changes. Follow database/README.md and the shared Compose/.env.example. Proposed schema c11_kpi_analytics needs database-owner agreement. Write only its own read model/receipts and read operational data through owner interfaces. Use UTC-stamped dbmate migrations under database/migrations/ with working up/down; verify local up → rollback → up, never edit merged migrations or create a parallel Supabase history. Outside-pair review is required; Bruno applies merged develop migrations to shared Supabase. Never manually change shared tables or commit secrets. Agree retention, keys and access before DDL.

All examples are synthetic. Tests read the component-owned examples and validate Pydantic shape, null/zero, coverage, timestamps and staleness; they do not prove authorisation, persistence, deduplication or integration. Run repository-root npm run contracts:lint, npm run contracts:build, then backend uv run pytest, uv run ruff check . and uv run ruff format --check .. Component-specific invariants belong in backend/component tests. The service must enforce records.length <= the requested limit, numeric coverage comparisons, authorisation and state transitions. OpenAPI checks do not validate events/internal Markdown. Future behaviour is #16; agreement/review comes before runtime work. Prepared with AI assistance for Jolin; no producer agreement, deployment or completed paired implementation is claimed.

docs.title: C12 Simulation and Replay: internal interfaces (UC12)
docs.text:
Status: contract proposal; no runtime endpoint is implemented here. Follows #35/#46; HTTP publication is tracked by #48. Pair: Jolin + Qingyuan. Requested HTTP reviewers: Julian (Antel0p3) and Oscar (OscarGomezGonzalezz). AI-assisted preparation for Jolin; no completed paired work or UC12 handover is claimed.

The C01-facing API definitions, field schemas, examples and HTTP failures now live in openapi.yaml. Browser calls are not internal interfaces. Transport proposals (paths, paging, idempotency receipts and error envelopes) need consumer review. In-process Result<T>, C02 context and typed models remain unchanged; HTTP adapters translate them rather than redefining shared types. Event contracts stay in events.yaml.

docs.title: C01 HTTP operations
docs.text:
Logical operation HTTP contract startSimulation POST /api/v1/simulation-runs listRuns GET /api/v1/simulation-runs startReplay POST /api/v1/replay-sessions getReplayFrame (read-only polling) GET /api/v1/replay-sessions/{sessionId} controlReplay POST /api/v1/replay-sessions/{sessionId}/controls

The OpenAPI file defines authentication, fields, status mapping, timeline controls, idempotent HTTP retries and transport-only run paging. Session ID comes from the control path, then the adapter supplies it to the existing ReplayControl model. State/range/cursor validation remains required in the service implementation. Existing typed value models remain in backend/app/components/c12_simulation_replay/contracts.py.

docs.title:
recordSimulationEvent(runId, record: RecordingRecord) → Result

Caller: trusted isolated simulation recorder, never a public replay session. runId is a required UUID v4 matching record and event. Example: record. Its SyntheticDeliveryCompleted event from C12-fixture is deliberately synthetic, not a production event declaration. Real payloads use the original producer's schema; see events.yaml.

Persist full ordered outcomes independent of coalesced city notifications. Sequence is contiguous/one-based per run; same eventId returns original receipt, conflicting ID/sequence fails. Receipt DTO fields remain unagreed; the model does not enforce cross-record ordering/durability. Failures: Invalid (wrong run/scope/payload), Forbidden, Conflict, Unavailable (no partial recording).

advanceReplay(sessionId, expectedCursor) → Result

Caller: trusted replay scheduler. sessionId: UUID v4, required; expectedCursor: nonnegative strict integer, required. Applies the next recorded outcome exactly once; completed at range end. Failures: Invalid, Forbidden, NotFound, Conflict, Unavailable. Interrupted recording reads pause without cursor advance. This is a provided scheduler boundary; checkpoint loading/reconstruction helpers are component implementation details and are not additional public contracts.
Internal recording/checkpoint values
docs.text:
RecordingRecord (required fields): runId (UUID v4), sequence (strict integer >=1), simulationTime (UTC timestamp), event (shared EventEnvelope from the same simulation run). Example: recording.

Checkpoint (required fields): runId (UUID v4), cursor (strict integer >=0), simulationTime (UTC timestamp), stateRef (nonempty string, at most 200 characters), stateSha256 (64 lowercase hexadecimal characters). Example: checkpoint. These are internal values, not C01 endpoints.

The shared envelope is defined by backend/app/shared/contracts.py; producer event payloads are referenced in events.yaml, never copied into the HTTP catalog. TimeRange/Indicator are reused from C11's Python module. C12's namespaced OpenAPI value schemas are exports of those same models for the aggregate catalog, not new metric formulas or producer event definitions.

docs.title: Recording, reproducibility and checkpoint semantics
docs.text:
The manifest and checkpoint reference immutable objects. Fixture refs/hashes are placeholders, not verified real objects. Retain versioned scenario/configuration, generator version and deterministic inputs; seed alone does not establish reproducibility. Runtime must verify object integrity.

Cursor is the last applied sequence, zero for initial state. A checkpoint is the state after its cursor. Apply full source outcomes by sequence even at equal timestamps. Coalesced CityStateUpdated notifications cannot replace a complete source recording. Validate sequence gaps, duplicate conflicts and checkpoint/range consistency at runtime; individual models only validate shape/run scope.

Replay loads a checkpoint at/before the selected start and all essential outcomes through the selected range. Missing configuration, checkpoint or essential event makes that range unreconstructable; return CannotReplay and availableRanges. After a read interruption retain the last successful state/cursor; resume retries the next unread event exactly once.

docs.title: Timeline transport
docs.text: The C01 play/pause/resume/seek/stop state table and HTTP error mapping now belong to c12ControlReplay in openapi.yaml. Scheduler natural completion and read interruption still use the same recorded-state/cursor guarantees. Speed is presentation pacing only. Its >0 and <=16 bound needs C01 review; seek does not rerun today's planner. Stop/completion returns the existing frame; additional final-summary fields need a future agreed DTO.

docs.title: Required interfaces and isolation
docs.text:
Provider Required contract/use Status C02 Authenticated roles/provider/run scope; recheck session ownership on every command. Owner definition pending; payload identity is not authorisation. C04/C05/C06/C08/C10 Durable run-scoped source outcomes, plans/decisions and audit/record data as appropriate. Producer definitions and exact subscriptions must be agreed, not copied into C12. C10 access may be internal rather than an event. C06 Original observation recording and historical state as needed. C06 internal.md owns getCitySnapshot; notifications alone are not a full recording. C10 Authorised historical decision/evidence retrieval for runId + decisionId. C10 owns selector and missing-evidence outcome; existing C12 DecisionSelector is only a consumer-side proposal pending #13/#34. C11 Recorded Indicator values in saved outcomes. Reuse the value model; replay must not call current queryKPIs to replace history. C01/infrastructure View routes, pacing/page bounds, run storage, checkpoints, retention and isolated credentials. Agree before implementation.

Use recorded decisions, original KPI values and C10's original saved evidence. Do not query today's C09 corpus for replacement evidence; show missing evidence explicitly. DecisionSelector(runId, decisionId) in C12's typed models does not redefine an authoritative C10 API. Method names/signatures belong to C10.

Simulation generation may use isolated simulated adapters. Playback cannot create operational activity: read-only recorded-data credentials, separate writable session storage, and no credentials/network route for live plan/resource writes, vehicle commands, agent negotiation or broker publishing. events.yaml describes the recorder's receive boundary, not a replay publication capability. Integration tests with real restricted replay credentials must prove denied live writes/publication before calling replay integrated.
